claim: P2P can be re-enabled on CMP 170HX: three bayley/cmpunlocker driver patches plus the regkey ForceP2P=0x11 make cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer 1 in both directions, verified by cuMemcpyPeer and NCCL reporting 'via P2P/CUMEM'.
stance_target: The repo's absolute claim that there is no P2P on this box and that EP/TP are therefore ruled out by the fabric
scope_conditions: 2x CMP 170HX on separate root complexes, EPYC 7443 / ROMED8-2T, cmpunlocker master 6c442ee + bayley patches 0011/0013/0015 at commit 5a7bb4b, IOMMU off
quoted_support: What works here is a regkey plus three driver patches on top of cmpunlocker. ... Verify: cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer is 1 in both directions; cuMemcpyPeer works both ways; with NCCL_DEBUG=INFO you see Channel NN/0 : 0[0] -> 1[1] via P2P/CUMEM in both directions.

claim: By default, two cards on separate root complexes report cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer 0 and the GSP capabilities report GPU_NOT_SUPPORTED.
stance_target: The repo's observation that P2P is unavailable out of the box
scope_conditions: 2x CMP 170HX on separate root complexes, stock cmpunlocker install
quoted_support: Two cards on separate root complexes default to no P2P: cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer is 0, and the GSP capabilities report GPU_NOT_SUPPORTED.

claim: With P2P working, vLLM TP=2 prefill is about 1.8 to 1.9 times faster than without P2P, on Gen2.
stance_target: The repo's claim that tensor parallelism is categorically ruled out by the fabric rather than by the missing P2P capability
scope_conditions: 2x CMP 170HX, vLLM 0.30.0 TP=2, Gen2 link, W4A16 MoE model
quoted_support: Result: vLLM TP=2 prefill is about 1.8 to 1.9 times faster than without P2P, on Gen2.

claim: After the unlock each card reports 64 GB, 74 SMs and trains at PCIe Gen2 x16.
stance_target: The repo's 64 GB-per-card and Gen2 claims, and shows that width can reach x16 on a suitable board
scope_conditions: 2x CMP 170HX on ROMED8-2T with Above 4G Decoding and Resizable BAR enabled, cmpunlocker master 6c442ee
quoted_support: Result: each card reports 64 GB, 74 SM, and the link trains at PCIe Gen2 x16.

claim: cmpunlocker master 6c442ee re-enables reserved TPCs to give 74 SMs per card, whereas release v0.4 gives 70 SMs.
stance_target: The claim that the effective SM count of the card is a tunable, which changes achievable TFLOPS
scope_conditions: cmpunlocker master 6c442ee ('Add more SMs', PR #55) versus v0.4
quoted_support: Use master 6c442ee or newer: it opens RECONFIG_PLM and re-enables the reserved TPCs, 70 to 74 SM per card (check with torch multi_processor_count; dmesg shows SM-RECONFIG GPCn). v0.4 gives 70 SM.

claim: The 250 W card can be cross-flashed to NVIDIA's 300 W VBIOS (92.00.6D.00.0A), raising memory clock to 1728 MHz and SM max to 1695 MHz.
stance_target: The niconiconi review's claim that VBIOS modding is impossible due to signature checks - flashing a signed vendor image works even though editing does not
scope_conditions: nvflash 5.867 on Linux, TechPowerUp image #268495, one nvflash operation per card per cold boot
quoted_support: Our two cards came with different VBIOS: 92.00.67.00.01 (250 W, memory 1458 MHz, SM max 1410 MHz) and 92.00.6D.00.0A (NVIDIA's 300 W "OC mining" image, memory 1728 MHz, SM max 1695 MHz). ... Result: both cards 6D, 64 GB unlock unaffected, memory 1728 MHz, max 300 W.

claim: Thermal headroom is the binding constraint above 200 W: 200 W plateaus at 77 C, 225 W at 83-84 C with no margin, and 250 W runs away at +6 C/min.
stance_target: Whether the 250 W cap in the repo's hardware table is achievable in a workstation chassis
scope_conditions: 2x CMP 170HX, one 75 mm blower per card at 100% duty, open case, gpu-burn on both cards simultaneously
quoted_support: Our thermal test (both cards under gpu-burn at once, blowers at 100%, open case): 200 W plateaus at 77 C, 225 W at 83-84 C (no margin), 250 W runs away (+6 C/min, no plateau). We run 200 W.

claim: A +200 MHz GPC V/F offset is stable under real vLLM load at 200 W (~1600-1650 MHz), while +250 MHz hung a card with Xid 175 within seconds.
stance_target: How much clock headroom the cards have at a fixed power cap, which sets achievable TFLOPS
scope_conditions: 6D VBIOS, nvmlDeviceSetGpcClkVfOffset, sustained bf16 GEMM and real vLLM load
quoted_support: Under a sustained bf16 GEMM at 200 W: +0 about 1385 MHz, +200 about 1500 MHz, +250 about 1525 MHz. ... +250 hung one card within seconds under real vLLM load (Xid 175 GSP RPC timeout, then Xid 154 ...). +200 is our serving point: clean under real load, about 1600-1650 MHz at 200 W.

claim: This deployment keeps the model's PLE / n-gram tables in host RAM (~128 GB) via VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1, because leaving them on the GPU causes an OOM.
stance_target: The repo's Memory Grafting claim that large frozen Engram lookup tables can live outside VRAM and thereby make a bigger model fit
scope_conditions: vLLM 0.30.0, W4A16 MoE (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), 2x CMP 170HX, 256 GB DDR4 host RAM
quoted_support: VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1 keeps the PLE / n-gram tables in host RAM (about 128 GB; budget roughly 180 GB for the container/host). Without it you get a GPU OOM.

claim: Prefill throughput without P2P is flat at ~2500 tok/s across 8k to 128k context, while with P2P it starts at 4634 tok/s (70 SM) and declines only slightly to 4486 at 128k.
stance_target: The repo's claim that a communication-bound fabric produces flat, length-independent throughput
scope_conditions: vLLM 0.30 TP=2, W4A16 MoE, both cards capped at 200 W, 3-rep medians

claim: The regkey ForceP2P=0x11 alone, without the three driver patches, was never verified sufficient - an earlier version of the writeup claimed it was and that claim was withdrawn.
stance_target: How reproducible the P2P enablement is, which bounds how much weight the training-feasibility analysis should put on it
quoted_support: Not tested: whether the regkey alone, without the three patches, is enough. An earlier version of this gist said so; that was not verified.

claim: The initial P2P setup was not reproducible for some users, and the revised recipe pins exact commits and adds UEFI/kernel requirements (Above 4G Decoding, Resizable BAR, IOMMU off, pure UEFI boot).
stance_target: Whether the P2P result generalises to the repo's box, which the repo's documentation does not address
scope_conditions: ROMED8-2T UEFI-only board, Proxmox VE kernel 7.0.14-pve, LXC containers
quoted_support: Update 2026-10-02. The initial setup here was not reproducible for some people (P2P did not come up). This is the revised setting: amogh's cmpunlocker as the base, patched selectively with three P2P patches from bayley/cmpunlocker, pinned to exact commits

claim: MTP speculative decoding acceptance is about 80% on code and 36% on prose, and decode is mostly memory-bound so the higher memory clock helped more than the extra SMs.
stance_target: Whether the box's decode throughput is bandwidth-limited, which is consistent with the repo's premise
scope_conditions: vLLM 0.30 TP=2 with P2P, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, MTP 4
quoted_support: MTP acceptance about 80% on code, 36% on prose throughout. Decode is mostly memory-bound, so the 6D memory clock helped it and the extra SMs alone did not.
